chapter: Chicago clubs, entertainers and tent shows
title: How Chicago musicians regarded New York
summary: Chicago musicians had no dream of going to New York, finding its music more sophisticated and classical, though Armstrong was a sensation there.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Now, okay getting back to 1926 and Chicago. How did musicians in Chicago regard New York, was that the --
There was no big dream of getting to New York?

No big dream of getting to New York at all. Because New York was entirely different type of -- their music was entirely different. And it didn't have the feeling of the music in Chicago. It was more sophisticated.
More classical than the music in Chicago.
Course Louie had gone to New York and was a sensation.
And that didn't make the other people want to go.
